answer: One concrete defence is a reputation bond that grows with proven work: each new agent starts with a thin layer of trust, like shale, and must earn thicker standing through attested tasks before it can move value. A sudden tide of fresh identities then hits a real cost, because every clone must redo the same slow work, and the network can spot the pattern when hundreds of accounts behave identically, like water cutting the same canyon. Sybils stay expensive while honest agents compound.
